sources.title: NRCan MRDEM-30 DTM
sources.vertical_accuracy: bare earth; built from HRDEM lidar where available, otherwise from regional DEMs (a few metres)

sources.notes: bare-earth DTM; outside Canada left as nodata; model area filled to 100.0%

sources.title: Ontario MNRF lake bathymetry (measured)
sources.vertical_accuracy: survey dependent; many surveys are historic (1950s-1990s) fish-habitat transects
sources.vertical_datum: depth below the water level at the time of the survey
sources.citation: Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources, Bathymetry Line and Bathymetry Point (Land Information Ontario), Open Government Licence - Ontario. https://geohub.lio.gov.on.ca/datasets/mnrf::bathymetry-line

sources.title: Estimated lake bathymetry (not measured)
sources.vertical_accuracy: not measured; estimated from lake shape and surrounding slope, depth errors of tens of percent or more
sources.vertical_datum: depth below the DEM water surface
sources.citation: Depth from distance to shore (Hollister, J.W., Milstead, W.B., 2010, Lake and Reservoir Management 26, 194-199) with the maximum depth predicted from the surrounding land slope (Hollister, J.W., Milstead, W.B., Urrutia, M.A., 2011, PLoS ONE 6(9), e25764), the method used for GLOBathy (Khazaei et al., 2022, Scientific Data 9, 36).

sources.title: Lake outlines (OpenStreetMap)
sources.citation: Feature geometry (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright

sources.title: Global depth to bedrock, 250 m (Shangguan et al., 2017)
sources.vertical_accuracy: Low: cross-validated RMSE of several to tens of metres; deep sedimentary basins are underestimated. Replace with borehole-derived surfaces when available.
sources.citation: Shangguan, W., Hengl, T., Mendes de Jesus, J., Yuan, H., Dai, Y. (2017). Mapping the global depth to bedrock for land surface modeling. Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems 9, 65-88. https://doi.org/10.1002/2016MS000686
sources.notes: absolute depth to bedrock in cm (BDTICM); model area filled to 99.0%
